access.admission: A device or private runner forwards a local port to the cache host listener under its own rds identity. The cache host agent admits that identity and allows only the cache listener as its TCP target. Host, ticket, port and admitted identities live in the private estate.

integrity: The cache returns upstream bytes unchanged and commits an object only after a complete download. Two documents are the cache's own: it generates the crates.io index config.json, and as it serves npm package documents, PyPI project pages and pub package documents it points download links that open a JSON string at the client's base address; hashes and every other value stay as upstream sent them. Clients keep their own digest and signature checks.

clients.limits: Gradle refuses plain-HTTP Maven repositories without an explicit opt-in, so Android engine artifacts need TLS in front of the forwarded port. Pub packages are a later increment.

routes.objects: Package documents in the representation the client accepts, the install document or the full document, revalidated and served with their tarball links pointed at this route of the client's base address; tarballs of exact published versions, which clients check against the integrity in the document.

clients.limits: A bun.lock written through the cache records the forwarded base in its tarball URLs, so create and update lockfiles against the public registry; bun install --frozen-lockfile with such a lockfile fetches its tarballs through the cache.

Audit, search, login and publish endpoints are not proxied; run npm without audit. A package-lock.json written through the cache records the forwarded base in its resolved URLs, so create and update lockfiles against the public registry; npm ci with such a lockfile replaces the registry host and fetches through the cache.

clients.limits: uv lock through the cache records the forwarded base in uv.lock, and uv treats a lockfile resolved against another index as outdated, so locked project syncs keep the public index.
Only the JSON form is served; a client that accepts only HTML pages gets 406.

routes.objects: Package documents of the hosted repository API, revalidated and served with their archive links pointed at this route of the client's base address; archives of exact published versions, which pub checks against the archive_sha256 in the document.

clients.limits: pubspec.lock records the forwarded base as the hosted URL, and dart pub get --enforce-lockfile refuses a lockfile resolved against pub.dev, so locked builds keep the public repository. Security advisories are served with the package documents.
The same pub client and lockfile limits as dart pub get; Flutter SDK artifacts use the flutter route.

routes.objects: Release files of the Maven Central layout and their checksums; maven-metadata.xml is revalidated and snapshots are not served.

clients.limits: Gradle accepts a plain-HTTP repository only with isAllowInsecureProtocol = true. The selected candidate is plain HTTP on the literal 127.0.0.1 forwarded port over the authenticated, encrypted rds forward, not JVM HTTPS: the opt-in goes only on those cache URLs in a project-scoped init script, with no global disable, trust store or local CA, and with strict dependency verification against checksums that do not come from the cache. Private or authenticated repositories are not retargeted. Gradle probes repositories in order, so upstream 404s from the earlier ones are expected.
